tier_reason: The auto-generated README (last updated 2026-09-10) has wincode 0.6.1, prost 0.14.4, flatbuffers 25.12.19, capnp 0.27.0 and rmp-serde 1.3.1 rows in the same run. It states the compiler (rustc 1.100.0-nightly a36d05efa 2026-09-09, LLVM 23.1.1) and the CPU (AMD EPYC 9V74). The flags are in public code: tools/bencher/src/main.rs runs `cargo bench` with RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native', and Cargo.toml sets [profile.bench] lto = true. corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.100.0-nightly (a36d05efa 2026-09-09), LLVM 23.1.1; built with `cargo bench` (bench profile, lto = true in Cargo.toml) with RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native' set by tools/bencher/src/main.rs; criterion harness
corrections.claimed_speedup: On the 'log' dataset (page run 2026-09-10), wincode 0.6.1 serializes in 137.05 µs. The comparisons are prost 'encode' 731.23 µs (~5.3x; prost populate+encode is 1.8883 ms), flatbuffers 763.63 µs (~5.6x), capnp 480.15 µs unpacked (~3.5x) and rmp-serde (msgpack) 1.3179 ms (~9.6x). wincode deserializes in 1.4166 ms against 2.6802 ms for prost decode (~1.9x) and 2.3829 ms for rmp-serde (~1.7x). The same pattern holds on the other datasets: mesh serialize is 147.88 µs against 371.26 µs for flatbuffers and 5.8939 ms for prost encode. (derived from page data)
corrections.caveats: The headline numbers come from one dataset ('log') of a multi-dataset benchmark. wincode is not the fastest row: bitcode serializes log in 96.821 µs and deserializes it in 1.1452 ms. FlatBuffers and capnp have no deserialize figures on the page (†) because they are zero-copy formats. wincode is newer and less used outside the Solana ecosystem than postcard or bitcode. The benchmark host is a 2-core/4-thread Hyper-V VM.

notes: Every number in the record matches the log Raw data table in wincode's row. The prost figures are the 'encode'/'decode' variants. Flags are in the harness code, so the record's 'flags not itemized' was replaced. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0, 234 stars, not a fork, not archived. The last commit on default branch master is 2026-09-17; the record's 2026-09-23 is pushed_at, from a dependabot branch.

tier_reason: alecthomas/go_serialization_benchmarks is a well-known independent suite (1,624 stars). Its report/data.js has 200sc/bebop rows next to protobuf-go (official protocolbuffers/protobuf-go) and gogo/protobuf. All rows were regenerated in one run by maintainer matheusd in PR #178 (2025-07-04). The code is public (internal/serializers/bebop_200sc, generated from a .bop schema), but no CPU model or Go toolchain version is stated anywhere; the report says 'This report is user-generated'. That rules out A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: go_serialization_benchmarks report, SmallStruct. 200sc/bebop marshals in 94 ns/op (52 ns/op with buffer reuse), against 287 ns/op for protobuf-go (~3.1x, ~5.5x with reuse). It unmarshals in 112 ns/op (110 with reuse), against 356 ns/op (~3.2x). The margin over gogo/protobuf is smaller: 115 ns/op marshal (~1.2x) and 166 ns/op unmarshal (~1.5x). The 'capnproto' row (2181/364 ns/op) is the old third-party glycerine/go-capnproto, not the official capnproto Go library. (derived from page data)
corrections.caveats: This is a Go implementation of the Bebop format, distinct from the canonical https://github.com/6over3/bebop repo already catalogued (not a fork; its README credits 6over3/bebop and documents incompatibilities with the original compiler). The report states no CPU or Go version, and results are user-generated per the report page, so the tier is capped at B. The suite encodes time.Time at 100 ns precision. The independent wellquite.org/bebop Go implementation benchmarks almost identically (95/118 ns/op).

notes: Every number matches the 200sc/bebop, protobuf-go and capnproto rows in data.js. Context added: gogo/protobuf is a much closer competitor, and the capnproto row is glycerine/go-capnproto v1. Metadata checked: Apache-2.0, 83 stars, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-05-08 (active).

tier_reason: The benc and benc/usafe rows sit in alecthomas/go_serialization_benchmarks report/data.js, a well-known independent suite (1,624 stars), next to protobuf-go and gogo/protobuf. benc's author added the entry (PR #125), but the current report was regenerated in one run by maintainer matheusd (PR #178, 2025-07-04). The code is public (internal/serializers/benc/benc.go), but no CPU model or Go version is stated, so it is not A.

corrections.workload: Marshal/unmarshal of goserbench.SmallStruct (Name, BirthDay, Phone, Siblings, Spouse, Money) in the go_serialization_benchmarks harness. The serializer is hand-written field-by-field code on benc's std primitives (api_kind 'manual'), not bencgen-generated code.
corrections.claimed_speedup: go_serialization_benchmarks report, SmallStruct. benc marshals in 81 ns/op (80 for benc/usafe), against 287 ns/op for protobuf-go (~3.5x). It unmarshals in 103 ns/op (41 ns/op for benc/usafe with unsafe string aliasing), against 356 ns/op (~3.5x; ~8.7x unsafe). Against gogo/protobuf (115/166 ns/op) the margin is ~1.4x marshal and ~1.6x unmarshal. (derived from page data)
corrections.caveats: Same shared report page: CPU model and Go version are not stated (the report says it is user-generated), capping the tier at B. The benchmarked serializer is hand-written primitive calls (api_kind 'manual'), close to the suite's own hand-rolled 'baseline' row (163 ns/op total vs benc 184). It is not the schema/codegen path with forward/backward compatibility that benc advertises. The 41 ns/op unmarshal uses unsafe string aliasing. Low star count means limited validation beyond this one shootout.

notes: Every number matches the benc and benc/usafe rows in data.js; the row is spelled 'benc/usafe' on the page. The comparison is not like-for-like: manual encoding vs protobuf-go codegen, and the gogo/protobuf margin is much smaller. Metadata checked: MIT, 42 stars, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2025-05-17 (~16 months ago, so stale is correct).
